# Quantifiable Metrics for Kubernetes Upgrade Validation

Citation-backed analysis of what metrics exist for validating software upgrades in operator-deployed Kubernetes platforms — and what doesn't exist despite being expected.

**Last revised:** 2026-04-20

## TL;DR

The Kubernetes ecosystem relies primarily on **binary pass/fail gates** rather than continuous metrics for upgrade validation. No platform publishes P95/P99 upgrade duration SLOs. No platform measures rollback success rate (DORA counts rollbacks as failures). Conformance tests cover only ~5-6% of the e2e suite. CSV "Succeeded" doesn't guarantee operator health.

The most quantitative metrics come from three areas: **data integrity** (etcd checksums, PostgreSQL `checksum_failures`, CockroachDB MOLT Verify), **workload continuity** (kube-state-metrics PDB and restart gauges), and **OpenShift CI** (95%/70%/<1% pass rate thresholds).

## Key Metrics Summary

| Dimension | Best Available Metric | Type | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data integrity | PostgreSQL `checksum_failures` [3], etcd hash check every 1 min [1] | Continuous | Checksums miss internal structures [2] [10] |
| Functional smoke | CNCF conformance 100% pass [13], OpenShift 95% [14] | Threshold | Conformance = ~5-6% of e2e suite [12] [16] |
| Upgrade duration | OpenShift CVO 60-120 min formula [20] | Range | No P95/P99 SLOs anywhere |
| Rollback | DORA Change Failure Rate ~5% [30] [69] | Continuous % | Rollback itself not measured; most platforms don't support it [32] [33] |
| Workload continuity | `kube_poddisruptionbudget_status_pod_disruptions_allowed` [37] | Gauge | PDBs only cover eviction API [36] |
| Version skip | Kubelet N-3 skew policy [42] | Binary | No failure rate data for skip vs sequential |
| API compatibility | `apiserver_requested_deprecated_apis` [49] | Gauge | Static tools miss runtime behavioral changes |
| Operator lifecycle | `csv_succeeded` (0/1) [59] | Binary | CSV Succeeded ≠ operator healthy [64] |

## Decision Framework

1. **Start with Tier 1 metrics** — they're free with Prometheus + kube-state-metrics: pod restart rates, PDB status, deprecated API usage, CSV health.
2. **Add pre/post-upgrade conformance testing** via Sonobuoy and deprecated API scanning via Pluto/Kubent.
3. **Track DORA Change Failure Rate** to measure upgrade reliability over time.
4. **Define your own thresholds** — the ecosystem provides metrics but not targets. OpenShift's 95%/70%/<1% thresholds [14] are a reasonable starting model.
5. **Don't rely on rollback** — most platforms don't support it, and K8s 1.33's two-step rollback [29] only works before version finalization.
